This was a simple weighted-average question that I answered correctly. The core mechanics (locating "Total U.S. Federal Securities" in the Treasury Bulletin, weighted average with 2x weight on one period) are straightforward arithmetic. There's no existing skill specifically for weighted-average questions, but the question was simple enough that it didn't expose any non-obvious parsing or arithmetic pitfall.

The one mildly generalizable thing is the weighted-average formula convention itself — "give the 1981 value twice the weight" means (1×V1980 + 2×V1981)/3, not /2. But that's a basic arithmetic convention that didn't trip me up and a future agent shouldn't need a skill to derive. The data sourcing ("Total U.S. Federal Securities" / "Total public debt and guaranteed securities" from the federal securities table at February month-ends) is already covered conceptually by the existing FD-1 and general Treasury Bulletin skills.

Nothing genuinely new and generalizable came up here — it was a clean, correct answer on a basic weighted-average over two clearly-labeled federal securities values.

No skill needed.
